stories.title: Los Angeles Unified switches off Google AI Overviews on student devices
stories.note: Original reporter is AP (not fetched); cited TNW, which reports AP's facts. Google/education angle, not chip thread.

articles.title: Los Angeles schools switch off Google's AI Overviews on student laptops

facts.fact: Los Angeles Unified, the second-largest school district in the US, has switched off AI Overviews in Google search on student devices, the Associated Press reported.
The district has about half a million students and made no formal announcement.
LAUSD said it had "temporarily suspended" the feature to keep students' experience "age-appropriate and safe."
Earlier this month, Google said it would switch off Gemini and search for K-12 students by default, leaving schools to turn each one on.
Google won't offer search without its AI features; schools that reject AI entirely will lose search, Google's education chief Chris Phillips told The New York Times.
More than 540 employees and contractors have signed a petition asking Google to let schools keep search without AI.
In July, Common Sense Media called Google's AI search an "unacceptable risk" for students.
Fairfax County Public Schools in Virginia has built plug-ins that remove AI summaries; some districts are looking at Bing and DuckDuckGo.
Google is testing a "guided learning" tool that walks students through problems step by step.

stories.title: Bloomberg: restricted Nvidia Blackwell rack pledged for a $14M loan at Shanghai site linked to Megaspeed founder
stories.note: Same Nvidia/China chip thread as several posts in last 14 days (follow-up, not exact repeat). Original is Bloomberg (not fetched); cited TNW.

articles.title: Nvidia Blackwell chips pledged for $14M loan at Huang-linked site

facts.fact: Two Chinese companies installed Nvidia's restricted Blackwell chips at a Shanghai data centre linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reported on Friday.
Shanghai Shuoyao pledged a GB300 NVL72 rack to secure a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank.
Bloomberg ran the rack's serial number through a public warranty database, which showed Taiwan's Gigabyte built the rack.
A second company, Shanghai Kezhan, described a GB200 server at the same site and also listed 32 servers with H200 chips.
Alice Huang founded Megaspeed in 2023; the Singapore company became Nvidia's largest customer in Southeast Asia and is under US investigation over suspected chip smuggling.
The US blacklisted Megaspeed this week, and then Alibaba's Singapore unit.
Bloomberg said it has no evidence that Megaspeed itself sent Nvidia hardware to the site; Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing in the US probe.
Local media have said the site could house up to 800,000 servers.
Shipping Blackwell to China has always required a US licence, and President Donald Trump has said he does not want Blackwell chips going to China.

stories.title: Belgium's Wallonia orders Google to halt data centre construction near Charleroi
stories.note: Europe angle; Google. Sources VRT/Belga/Greenpeace via TNW.

articles.title: Greenpeace: 'Tech giants are not above the law' as Google site halted

facts.fact: The Walloon Region has ordered Google to stop building its data centre near Charleroi in Belgium.
Work had carried on for months at the site in Farciennes and Aiseau-Presles without a valid permit.
About 300 construction workers were on the site when the order came on Thursday.
Google's original permit, granted in 2024, covered three data centres cooled by air; in 2025 the company merged two buildings into one and switched to cooling with water from the Sambre river.
The Walloon administration approved the amended permit in April 2026; after residents appealed, the infrastructure minister revoked it in August.
The request covered 600 cubic metres of river water an hour, and less than a quarter would have gone back into the river, according to Belga.
On 17 October Google asked Belgium's Council of State to annul and suspend the minister's decision; a public hearing is set for 7 January.
"Tech giants are not above the law," said Nadia Cornejo, a Greenpeace Belgium spokesperson.

stories.title: Xpeng to mass-produce Iron humanoid robot from January 2027
stories.note: China robotics; sources CNBC/Bloomberg TV via TNW.

articles.title: Xpeng says its Iron humanoid could be doing chores in one or two years

facts.fact: Chinese EV maker Xpeng will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid robot in January 2027 and train it as a store assistant first.
Co-president Brian Gu told CNBC it could be doing household chores in "one or two years."
The robot has 76 degrees of freedom and more than 1,500 touch sensors.
It runs on three of Xpeng's own Turing AI chips, the same family it puts in its cars.
Xpeng's new production line is designed to finish one every 2.5 minutes at full speed.
Xpeng aims to sell "tens of thousands" of Iron robots in 2027, with public sales from the second quarter, Gu told Bloomberg TV.
Xpeng's robotics unit raised more than $900M in August ahead of the production run.
Morgan Stanley expects China to ship 50,000 humanoids this year.

stories.title: AI shopping agents handle just 0.4% of online orders, Bain finds, on Black Friday
stories.note: Muse mentioned; related to 11-24 Meta Muse UK post but different angle. Sources CNBC/Fortune/Bloomberg/Guardian via TNW.

articles.title: AI shopping agents handle just 0.4% of online orders, Bain finds

facts.fact: Shoppers spent a record $7.1bn online on Thanksgiving, up 10.4%, and Adobe expects $12.9bn on Black Friday itself.
Purchases made by AI agents made up 0.4% of global e-commerce transactions and 0.2% of their value, according to Bain & Co research.
A Morning Consult poll for Visa found 54% of adults have used AI for at least one shopping task, but only 23% trust generative AI to make payments for them.
Visa sent 22 AI models on 15 shopping tasks earlier this month, and they failed 42.8% of their runs; in more than half of failed runs, the agent still bought something.
About half of big retailers and popular brands do not let AI assistants shop their sites, according to London software firm Human Forward.
Amazon blocked Muse from its store in September and is suing Perplexity over the shopping agent in its Comet browser.
Best Buy's terms state it is "not responsible for conduct, errors, actions, or inaction by any Digital Agent."
Muse reached 10 million users in the US and Canada about six weeks after its September launch, Bloomberg reported.

stories.title: Huawei founder Ren Zhengfei tells NYT to pass on thanks to Trump for pushing China to self-reliance
stories.note: Chip-curb thread adjacent. Original is NYT (not fetched); cited TNW.

articles.title: Huawei's Ren Zhengfei on Trump: 'Pass on our thanks to him'

facts.fact: Huawei founder Ren Zhengfei spoke to The New York Times at Huawei's Shenzhen headquarters in October; the paper published the interview on Thursday.
"Pass on our thanks to him, and also share the story of the Trump Corridor as well," Ren told the Times.

The interview ran two days after a federal jury in New York convicted Huawei of conspiring to steal trade secrets and of bank fraud linked to Iran; Huawei said the verdicts were "without legal or factual merit."
Huawei now spends more than $27bn a year on research and development, according to the Times.
Huawei will make less than 4% as much AI computing power as Nvidia this year, Epoch AI estimates.
Its most powerful chip, the Ascend 950, delivers about half the performance of Nvidia's H100, which began shipping in 2022.
Ren said China would eventually overtake the US in chips: "It's just a matter of time."

stories.title: Nvidia tells Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia
stories.note: Same chip-curb thread as three posts in 14 days and Nvidia posted 11-24 (-10 if counted). Fresh angle: Nvidia itself enforcing. Covered by etnews, heise, TechCrunch. Evening-pick risk: same company.

articles.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
Nvidia stoppt offenbar Lieferungen von KI-Servern an einige Länder Südostasiens

facts.fact: According to the WSJ, Nvidia told manufacturing partners including Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia for an unspecified period.
Nvidia is assessing whether its regional partners are meeting US export requirements.
Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers in those countries, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed earlier this month.
The Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China's AI computing power.
heise cites the Financial Times, which relies on three people familiar with the matter, for the orders to Dell and Supermicro.
In 2025 Nvidia's Singapore subsidiary recorded $104 billion in revenue, up 72% from the prior year (heise).
It is unclear which AI chips the pause covers and whether it is time-limited (heise).
The US Commerce Department gave cloud providers a 90-day deadline to obtain a licence proving no sanctioned entities are among their customers; a cloud manager says nobody knows how to apply (heise).
Nvidia declined to comment; Dell and Supermicro did not respond to heise's requests.

stories.title: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in an AI-first restructuring
stories.note: Used by morning post; do not pick.

articles.title: SAP, AI 중심 구조조정 추진…최소 1만명 감원 검토

facts.fact: SAP is drawing up plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs as a result of its AI-first strategy, Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter.
SAP did not deny the plans and spoke of 'continuous reviews of the organisation'.
10,000 would be nearly a tenth of SAP's 110,730 employees worldwide (as of end of September).
SAP cut 10,000 jobs in 2024, mostly through voluntary departures, and has since added about 15,000 jobs.
All SAP departments were told to report where positions can be cut; programming, product support and sales are expected to be hit hardest.
SAP calls itself Europe's most valuable software company (heise: 'wertvollstes Softwareunternehmen Europas').
IG Metall criticised the September agreement with the German works council as setting severance amounts rather than protecting jobs.
AI타임스: the size and timing of the cuts are not final and could change in talks with employee representatives.
AI타임스: since July SAP has limited new hiring mainly to core AI roles and cut costs such as travel; the 2024 restructuring cost about 3 billion euros.
AI타임스: Microsoft, Oracle and Salesforce have also recently announced thousands of job cuts citing AI efficiency.

stories.title: Bank of England governor warns unreleased frontier AI could threaten encryption; Aaronson says labs hold crypto 'bombshells'
stories.note: Not covered by reference accounts. Good explainer angle (financial regulators now cite AI, not only quantum, for crypto risk). Aaronson claim is unverified (TNW says so); present as claim. BoE detail via AI타임스 (citing FT), not read in English original.

articles.title: 영국 중앙은행 총재 "미공개 최첨단 AI, 암호화 체계 위협 가능성"
AI labs sit on 'one or more bombshells' in cryptography, Aaronson says

facts.fact: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey was asked on the 26th, after the Financial Stability Report, about rumours that an AI model able to break existing cryptography already exists.
Bailey said of Anthropic's Mythos, which appeared in April, 'Mythos is now a past model' and said model generations now turn over in one to two months.
He said that in AI developers' own words, 'we are in a section of an exponential curve', and strongly backed developers' caution about releasing the latest models.
He did not say what the unreleased models can do.

For the first time, the Bank of England formally advised financial firms to prepare for crypto risks from AI progress, not only quantum computing, by mapping where cryptography is used and planning priority migrations.
Financial institutions had been preparing crypto migration for quantum computing targeting after 2030; AI maths progress may force that timeline earlier.
No AI company has so far published a concrete result that breaks existing cryptography.

Scott Aaronson wrote on his blog Wednesday that he is 'virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells' in cryptography; he does not know what they are. TNW has not independently verified the claims.

Aaronson said his certainty falls well short of 'Factoring in P' (a fast way to break RSA), and that Google's Wednesday paper with a new factoring algorithm has big theoretical results but nothing practical for breaking encryption.
On Tuesday OpenAI and Anthropic both published proofs of VP != VNP; OpenAI also posted a 111-page paper claiming the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4.

stories.title: Canada adds C$700M to its AI Compute Access Fund, favouring Canadian-owned clouds
stories.note: Not covered by reference accounts. Sovereign-compute angle, matches the EU sovereign tech fund post of 11-25 thematically. TNW only; one source.

articles.title: Canada adds C$700M to its AI compute fund, favouring home-grown clouds

facts.fact: Canada is adding C$700M to its AI Compute Access Fund, taking it to C$1B, up from C$300M, the government said on Thursday.
In the new phase the fund pays more when companies use computing owned and run in Canada, to create demand for local providers.
Evan Solomon, Canada's minister of artificial intelligence and digital innovation, said 'Canadian ideas need Canadian computing power'.
The first new round is open to health and life sciences projects.
More than C$52M goes to 45 companies from the first phase, bringing the total to over C$118M for 89 firms.
The money comes from Canada's national AI strategy, unveiled in June; Ottawa pledged to bring 500 megawatts of its own AI computing online.
In October Canada backed Cohere's C$7bn funding round.

stories.title: Dutch court hears bid to ban Meta's AI glasses; German consumer group also sues
stories.note: Follow-up to the 11-20 post (Dutch regulator warning); new angle is the court hearing and ruling by Dec 24. Source is AI타임스 citing Reuters (Reuters not read). Der Standard also ran a story (not read).

articles.title: 네덜란드 시민단체, 메타 AI 안경 판매 금지 요구…독일서도 법적 대응

facts.fact: A hearing was held on the 26th at the Amsterdam District Court in a civil suit against Meta and Ray-Ban parent EssilorLuxottica, per Reuters.
Plaintiffs are the Dutch Consumers' Association, Offlimits and The Firewall; they say the glasses breach European privacy law.
Offlimits and The Firewall also seek a sales ban; all demand technical measures against filming people unaware and an end to using recordings for AI training.
Meta argues the suit should be dismissed, noting an indicator light on the frame; EssilorLuxottica says it does not access or process footage and a ban would be excessive.
Meta and EssilorLuxottica sold more than 7 million smart glasses last year, about 80% of the global market.
The Dutch data protection authority advised consumers on the 19th not to buy six AI camera glasses it examined.
Germany's VZBV consumer federation announced legal action against Meta and Ray-Ban on the 24th.
The Dutch court will decide by December 24 at the latest; the ruling applies only to the Netherlands.

stories.title: 42 US state attorneys general move to stop Character.AI from auctioning users' private chats in bankruptcy
stories.note: Not covered by reference accounts. Auction scheduled Dec 1. One source (TechCrunch). The Verge covered it too (403).

articles.title: Character.AI's plan to auction off users' private chats challenged by state AGs

facts.fact: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai's bankruptcy case to stop the sale of user data including private conversations.
The AGs say the dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million US accounts, more than 2.1 million of them minors, plus data like IP addresses.
Character.ai filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October and had told consumers their personal information would not be sold.
The only disclosed bidder is Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, set up in Delaware on November 13, 2026; Character.ai picked it as base bid the next day; the auction is scheduled for December 1.
California, Colorado, New York and Connecticut chatbot safety laws take effect January 1, 2027.
California AG Rob Bonta said 'bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections'.
A separate proposed $20 million licensing deal with Disney has not received final court approval; Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai's remaining staff.

stories.title: Swiss cyber agency: AI-agent attacks hit 4 of 5 targets, including 3 critical infrastructure operators
stories.note: Not covered by reference accounts. Source is AI타임스 only (relaying BACS announcement; BACS not read). heise also ran a BSI (Germany) story on autonomous AI attacks, not read.

articles.title: 스위스 정부 "AI 에이전트 활용 사이버 공격 5건 확인…4건 침해 성공"
Swiss cyber chief: AI agents 'cannot get into a system' without a flaw

facts.fact: Five cyberattacks using AI agents occurred in Switzerland and four of them breached systems.
Targets included three critical infrastructure operators (power, water, telecoms among sectors named).
Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) announced the cases on the 24th and said on the 26th that 4 of 5 attacks recently identified succeeded.
The attackers' identity was not disclosed.
The agents probe for vulnerabilities themselves and decide next steps from results, using techniques security experts use for testing.
The number of such AI-agent tools available online has nearly doubled since October.
Authorities recommend fast security updates, multi-factor authentication and regular penetration tests.
Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) confirmed its first AI-agent cyberattacks in an advisory on Tuesday.
Director Florian Schütz said on Thursday the agency has five confirmed cases; three targeted critical infrastructure operators, and across all five attackers got into systems four times.
The NCSC wants companies to install critical security updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours of release.
The number of such agents reachable online has almost doubled since October, according to the NCSC.
